churn_resistance.rationale: Excellent layering — one data module, typed boundaries, constants and env handling centralized, no framework internals touched — so a framework or API upgrade would touch very few files. Small deductions for duplicated URL-param/sprite-template logic, the four-times-repeated not-found pattern, and the untyped upstream parsing that leaves the boundary half-guarded.

findings.issue: No devDependencies and no typecheck script: typescript is not installed, so the strict tsconfig and the boundary types in src/lib/types.ts are never verified by any command — future framework upgrades would silently drift.
findings.suggestion: Add a devDependency on typescript and a "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit" script, and run it before builds.

findings.issue: nitro is pinned to a pre-release line (^3.0.260903-beta); Nitro v3's RC (3.0.261029-rc, released 2026-10-29) documents breaking changes from beta, and a caret range on a prerelease will not pick the RC or a future stable release up automatically.
findings.suggestion: Track the v3 RC/stable deliberately once it lands and update the range; treat the beta→stable jump as a scheduled upgrade rather than an ambient drift.

findings.issue: Upstream fetches have no timeout or abort signal, so a hung PokeAPI request can hold a page render open indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Pass signal: AbortSignal.timeout(ms) to fetch and let the in-memory cache evict failed entries (the value.catch on line 56 already handles rejection).

findings.issue: The sprite URL template `${apiBase()}/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png` is built in two places.
findings.suggestion: Extract a sprite(id) helper next to card() so a media-path change is one edit.

findings.issue: Query-param handling is duplicated: a first() helper on the home route, an inline Array.isArray check on the pokemon route, and a separate URLSearchParams parse in the home preload.
findings.suggestion: Put a small param helper (single value from string | string[] | undefined) in src/lib/format.ts or a shared routing module and reuse it in both routes and preloads.

findings.issue: The Switch/Match null-check + NotFound fallback is copy-pasted across four route files (pokemon, moves, abilities, types).
findings.suggestion: Wrap it once, e.g. a <DataPage data={x} render={...}> component or a shared helper, so a change to the not-found flow is one edit.

findings.issue: Upstream payloads are typed as `any` inside the mapping functions, so the compiler guards only the app side of the boundary.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal payload interfaces (Species, Pokemon, Move, ...) at the fetch boundary so upstream shape changes surface as type errors instead of runtime ones.

summary: This app is on the current stable stack — SolidStart 2.1 on Vite 8 and Nitro v3, router 1.0, solid-js 1.9 — and uses every framework API in its documented current form (query + "use server" + createAsync, route.preload, HttpStatusCode, createHandler options). The data layer is cleanly isolated behind typed server functions, so framework or API upgrades touch very few files. The deductions are small and fixable: a prerelease nitro pin, no typecheck tooling to enforce the otherwise strict types, a few duplicated URL/sprite templates, and untyped upstream payloads at the fetch boundary.
